correctness.rationale: For coprime integers p,q>1 and s>1 coprime with pq, map a to x^q and b to y*x^p*y^{-1} from <a,b|a^p=b^q> to <x,y|x^{pq}=y^s>. The relation is respected because both pth and qth images equal k=x^{pq}, which is central. Quotient by central powers gives C_p*C_q to C_{pq}*C_s. Images x^q and y*x^p*y^{-1} have exact orders p,q and lie in distinct conjugates of the C_{pq} factor; alternating nonidentity syllables remain reduced when y words are inserted, so the quotient map is injective. Any kernel is therefore contained in the central <a^p>; its generator maps to k, which has infinite order under homomorphism x→s,y→pq to Z. Hence injective. Both full centers are these infinite cyclic powers, because quotient free products have trivial centers; a finite-order element of C_p*C_q has order dividing p or q, so cannot have order pq, while C_{pq}*C_s does have one. Thus groups are nonisomorphic. Example (p,q,s)=(2,3,5) gives G_{2,3}↪G_{6,5}. This proves sufficiency, not classification of all embeddings.
